kinds.explicit: Printed on the RDSO sheet and read from a displayed image of it (verification level says whether it was re-checked).
kinds.derived: Follows mathematically from printed notations or tables (the derivation is written out); not printed as such.
kinds.unverified: Printed, but the extraction marks it unclear, or it is on a page the extraction did not check, or the extraction says not to use it.
kinds.implementation: A rule of an existing implementation (aagento-bridge production code, this template): not RDSO content; recorded in the template.
kinds.engineer: A design choice an engineer makes and can change: not RDSO content; recorded in the template and in each bridge's config.

rules_of_use: A schedule value applies only to its own standard, fill height and span x height configuration; the five standards are NOT interchangeable (loading, track, construction and curvature differ: see each configuration).

No interpolation: the sheets give discrete configurations. The notes allow the IMMEDIATELY HIGHER span/height configuration for intermediate spans/heights (the note is cited per standard). For an intermediate FILL height the sheets say nothing: taking the next higher tabulated fill is an engineer's choice, recorded as such by the template.
RDSO guides geometry and validation; it never overrides an engineer's explicit input. A difference is reported with both values.
Values marked unverified are shown but never used to pass or fail a check.

kb_context.definition: floor_level = soffit_level - clear_height

kb_context.definition: soffit_level = seat_level + bearing_height

kb_context.definition: haunch ≥ 0.3 m — unverified; drawings in hand use 200

kb_context.name: Weep holes 1 m × 1 m staggered; lowest row placement
kb_context.definition: Weep holes at 1 m vertical and 1 m horizontal, staggered, in abutments, wing and return walls; the bottom row above LWL in flowing streams, 250 mm above bed otherwise, above FSL in canals.

kb_context.name: Vertical clearance above the design water level (by discharge)
kb_context.definition: Soffit minus the water level of the design discharge incl. afflux: 600 mm for 0–30 m³/s, 600–1200 pro rata for 31–300, 1500 for 301–3000, 1800 above.

kb_context.name: Pipe and box culverts: no vertical clearance (pressure conduits)
kb_context.definition: Syphons, pipe and box culverts are designed as pressure conduits; no clearance is required for them.

kb_context.name: Pipe / box culverts not where the bed is likely to scour
kb_context.definition: Pipe and box culverts on open foundations are built on a levelled, consolidated bed with lean concrete, and should not normally be provided where the bed is likely to be scoured.

kb_context.name: RCC box span > 3 m needs CAO(C) / CBE approval
kb_context.definition: RCC boxes for minor bridges up to 3 m span with adequate cushion; larger spans need CAO(C)/CBE approval (IRCM, quoted by a secondary source).

kb_context.name: Minimum earth cushion
kb_context.definition: No source in hand sets a minimum cushion or its datum; the documented 75 mm (RCR-VAL-007) is unverified.

kb_context.name: Minimum haunch
kb_context.definition: No source in hand sets a minimum haunch; the documented 300 mm (RCR-VAL-008) is unverified.

kb_context.name: Formation not below the top of a buried structure
kb_context.definition: A box or pipe is under the formation: formation level ≥ top of the structure (cushion ≥ 0).

kb_context.name: Rail above formation
kb_context.definition: The rail sits on the formation: rail level above formation level.

kb_context.name: Top of structure above soffit above floor above underside
kb_context.definition: top of the top slab > soffit > floor > underside of the bottom slab.

kb_context.name: Rail over formation (0.762 m is an assumption)
kb_context.definition: Rail level minus formation level depends on the rail, sleeper and ballast of each track; 0.762 m is a common assumption, not a rule.

kb_context.name: chain.pipe
kb_context.definition: A pipe crossing: the invert (written, or at the bed), the inside crown, the outside crown (what the cushion is measured from), the outside invert and the bedding courses under it.

kb_context.name: chain.slab
kb_context.definition: A slab deck on abutments and piers: the deck from its soffit (written, or from its top and depth, or from the bearing seat), the seat under it, the footings from the B.O.F. (or the bed and the embedment) and the courses under them. A bearing not read is none.

kb_context.name: KC-1: Rail level − formation level
kb_context.definition: Rail level − formation level

kb_context.name: KC-2: Barrel length
kb_context.definition: Barrel length

kb_context.name: KC-3: Minimum haunch
kb_context.definition: Minimum haunch

kb_context.name: KC-5: Earth cushion minimum and datum
kb_context.definition: Earth cushion minimum and datum

kb_context.name: Bed level
kb_context.definition: Level of the stream bed at the bridge; in a box on the railway convention, the top of the wearing course in the cells.

kb_context.name: Top of the wing / return wall (its coping)
kb_context.definition: The level top of a wing or return wall — the top of its coping where it has one.

kb_context.name: Floor (top of bottom slab) / pipe invert
kb_context.definition: Top face of a box's bottom slab (under any wearing course), or a pipe's inside invert.

kb_context.name: Formation level
kb_context.definition: Top of the railway embankment on which the ballast rests; free board is measured to it (IRBM 313).

kb_context.name: Rail level
kb_context.definition: Level of the top of the rail.

kb_context.name: Soffit level
kb_context.definition: Underside of the top slab / deck (the inside crown of a pipe). Vertical clearance is measured to it (IRBM 312).

kb_context.name: Top of the wing / return wall (its coping)
kb_context.definition: The level top of a wing or return wall — the top of its coping where it has one.

kb_context.name: Ballast bed
kb_context.definition: Ballast cushion under sleepers.

kb_context.name: Box barrel
kb_context.definition: The monolithic RCC box (all cells, walls, slabs, haunches) as one component.

kb_context.name: Earth cushion (fill over box/pipe)
kb_context.definition: Fill between top of box/pipe and formation.

kb_context.name: Return wall
kb_context.definition: Wall parallel to the track (perpendicular to the abutment) retaining embankment side fill.

kb_context.name: Toe wall
kb_context.definition: Small wall at toe of pitching/apron.

kb_context.name: Top slab
kb_context.definition: Roof slab of the box; carries cushion/ballast/track.

kb_context.name: Wearing course
kb_context.definition: Wearing coat over deck or box top / floor.

kb_context.name: Coping
kb_context.definition: Cap course on top of a wing/return wall or abutment, sometimes chamfered.

kb_context.name: Haunch
kb_context.definition: Triangular thickening at slab–wall junction inside a cell, written 'HAUNCH a X b'.

kb_context.name: Shear key
kb_context.definition: Key between precast box units or slab joints.

kb_context.name: Wing wall stem
kb_context.definition: Stem of a wing/return wall above its footing.
